angle: Demo content: a fictional queue library, used to preview the carousel layout.

threads.post:
example/tidequeue replaces a Redis-backed job queue with Postgres SKIP LOCKED.

Workers claim rows in one statement, so there is no second system to operate.
The cost: polling load grows with worker count, and LISTEN/NOTIFY only softens it.

Good fit below a few thousand jobs per second.
threads.reply:
The README benchmark runs on a single node with 32 workers; there is no figure for replicas or failover.

Source: https://github.com/example/tidequeue

tiktok.title: A job queue that is just Postgres
tiktok.description: Demo brief. tidequeue claims jobs with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the queue lives in the database you already run. Polling cost is the trade-off. #softwareengineering #postgres #backend

slides.heading: Your job queue can be a Postgres table
slides.body: tidequeue drops Redis and claims jobs with SKIP LOCKED.

slides.heading: How a worker claims a job
bullets: Jobs are rows with a state and a run_at column
A worker selects the oldest ready row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
Locked rows are invisible to other workers, no double claim
Commit marks the job done in the same transaction as your writes

slides.heading: The claim query
slides.code:
UPDATE jobs SET state = 'running'
WHERE id = (
  SELECT id FROM jobs
  WHERE state = 'ready' AND run_at <= now()
  ORDER BY run_at
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
  LIMIT 1
)
RETURNING id, payload;
slides.body: One round trip. No lease table, no visibility timeout.

slides.label: jobs per second in the README benchmark
slides.body: Single node, 32 workers, demo figure. Nothing published for replicas or failover.

slides.heading: Verdict
slides.body: A sound default when jobs must commit atomically with business writes and volume is moderate.
